drug_class: Blood thinner (anticoagulant) — specifically a Factor Xa inhibitor
purpose: Rivaroxaban is used to prevent or treat dangerous blood clots in your legs, lungs, or other parts of your body. It is also used to lower the risk of stroke in people who have an irregular heartbeat called atrial fibrillation. Additionally, it may be prescribed after hip or knee replacement surgery to prevent clots from forming.
how_it_works: Your blood naturally clots to stop bleeding when you get a cut, but sometimes clots form inside your blood vessels where they should not be. Rivaroxaban works by blocking a specific protein in your blood called Factor Xa, which is a key step in the clot-forming process. By blocking this protein, the medication makes it harder for dangerous clots to form or grow bigger.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bleeding more easily than usual — this can include cuts that take longer to stop bleeding, bruising more easily, nosebleeds, or heavier periods. You may also notice pink, red, or dark-colored urine, or red or black stools, which should be reported to your doctor right away.
warnings: Because this medicine thins your blood, it can cause serious or life-threatening bleeding. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can increase your risk of a stroke or clot. Tell all of your doctors and dentists that you take this medication before any procedure or surgery. Avoid activities with a high risk of injury. Some medications and supplements — including aspirin, ibuprofen, and certain herbal products like St. John's Wort — can interact with rivaroxaban and increase your bleeding risk, so always check with your pharmacist before starting anything new.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on why you are taking it. For atrial fibrillation or preventing strokes, a common dose is 20 mg once a day taken WITH your evening meal. For treating blood clots, you may start at 15 mg twice a day with food for the first 3 weeks, then switch to 20 mg once a day with your evening meal. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, and try to take it at the same time each day.
